docs.title: MaameDrone V1.0 carrier board
docs.text: MaameDrone V1.0 is a 95 x 116.5 mm, 2-layer carrier board that joins the Maame quadcopter's flight controller, Pi Zero companion computer and peripherals on one plate. It sits on the Holybro S500 frame. It holds a Kakute H7 V1.5 on its 30.5 mm M3 holes and a Pi Zero W face down on a 2x20 socket. Labelled headers take the GPS, telemetry radio, RC receiver, rangefinder and payload servo.

docs.title: What the board does
docs.text:
• Makes its own 5 V rail (5V_AUX): a TPS54360B buck, 3.5 A, fed from the 6S battery through a 2 A fuse and a TVS diode. It powers the Pi and the servo, so they never load the Kakute's regulator.
  • Breaks out the Kakute: a short Dupont harness from the Kakute's solder pads lands on four headers (J1, J23, J24, J25). From there the board routes UART1 to the Pi, UART4 to the radio, UART6 + I2C to the GPS, R3 to the receiver and I2C to the rangefinder.
  • Gives a fused battery output (J20) for an accessory, 2 A.
  • Shows status on 7 LEDs: both 5 V rails, plus five Pi-driven LEDs for companion, data and battery level.
  • Leaves spares: FC spares (T3, RSSI, buzzer, LED), Pi GPIO, Pi SPI, a spare I2C header and spare 5 V.

The ESC is not on this board. It sits on the frame's lower plate and its cable comes up through a slot to the Kakute. The battery's main current never passes through the carrier.

Item Value Revision V1.0, rev 1.0, design dated 2026-10-27 (git commit 333d49e) Size 95.0 x 116.5 mm, 6 mm corner radius, 2 layers Input 6S Li-ion or LiPo, 18 to 25.2 V (22.2 V nominal) Rails 5V_AUX 3.5 A (on-board buck) · 5V_FC (from the Kakute) · 3V3_FC (from the Kakute) · 3V3_PI (from the Pi) · VBAT OUT 2 A fused Assembly JLCPCB fits the 32 SMD parts; you hand-solder all headers, the Pi socket and the battery wires

Directions used on this site

Front or nose is the edge with the buck regulator and the "NOSE" arrow. Rear is the Pi's USB/HDMI edge. Left and right are seen from the top with the nose pointing away from you.

docs.title: Board at a glance
docs.text: All parts are on the top side. The front strip holds the 5 V buck and the status LEDs, the Kakute sits in the middle over the ESC slot, and the Pi Zero lies face down across the rear. Power and FC-bus sensors leave from the left edge; the radio, receiver and Pi expansion leave from the right.

docs.text: Every pin name on this render is printed on the real board's silkscreen.

docs.title: Bottom side

docs.title: Related files
docs.text:
• Board design (KiCad 10, git): the maame-autonomous-drone repo, commit 333d49e, with fab/ASSEMBLY_NOTES.md and the JLC fab files.
  • Project folder: maame/cover/ (moisture lid), maame/fab/ (hand-solder BOM, renders PDF), maame/ardupilot/ (Lua arming gate), maame/pi/ (Pi scripts).
  • The maame/carrier/ KiCad files and netlist.json in the project folder are the 27 Oct draft and do not match V1.0.

docs.title: Assembly and bring-up
docs.text: Build the board, prove the 5 V rail on a bench supply with nothing plugged in, then add the Kakute, the Pi and each peripheral one at a time.

docs.title: Soldering the board
docs.text:
1. Check the JLC-assembled board: look for bridges on U2's pins and check that D8, D9 and C1 sit the right way round.
  2. U1 Pi socket: tack one pin at each end, check it sits square and flat, then solder the rest. A tilted socket stops the face-down Pi seating.
  3. Kakute headers J1, J23, J24, J25, then the peripheral and spare headers you need (J8, J9, J10, J11, J13; J6, J7, J12, J17, J18 optional), then the J20 JST socket.
  4. J3 battery wires: 18 AWG, red to "+", black to "−". Leave the other ends free for now.
  5. Trim every lead underneath to 1.5 mm or less.

docs.title: Kakute harness
docs.text:
1. Solder 26–28 AWG wires to the Kakute pads named in the J1, J23, J24 and J25 tables.
  2. Leave B+, Vo, Vi, CAM and 9V unwired. They have no net on the board, and B+ on a signal pin would destroy parts.
  3. Crimp the other ends into Dupont housings in the same order as the headers, pin 1 to the square pad.
  4. Before plugging in, beep each wire from the Kakute pad to its header pin. Check the J1 rows aren't swapped: pin 1 is B+ (unwired), pin 2 Vo (unwired), pins 3 and 4 GND.

docs.title: First power-up
docs.text:
1. Bench supply on J3: about 20 V, current limit about 0.3 A, nothing plugged into any header. The AUX5V LED should light.
  2. Measure J6 pin 1 or J13: 5.0 to 5.1 V. If it is wrong, stop and check U2 and R10/R11 before going further.
  3. Kakute: plug in the harness, then power the Kakute as normal (USB or ESC). The FC5V LED lights when the Kakute's 5 V rail is up; whether USB alone powers that rail is unconfirmed. Measure 5 V on J10 pin 2.
  4. Pi: check the orientation twice (pin 1 at the right, rear row; SD right; USB/HDMI rear), then plug it in face down and power from J3. The Pi boots from 5V_AUX.
  5. Peripherals, one at a time, checking each in Mission Planner before the next: GPS (J8), then receiver (J10), then SiK (J9), then TF-Luna (J11), then servo (J13 power + Kakute M5 signal).
  6. Then connect J3 to the ESC's battery pads and do the full system check on the real battery: Pi ready message, arming gate, LEDs, and a servo and motor test with the props off.

Tip

If the barometer reports "unable to initialise" after you add an I2C device, unplug the device: a wrong SDA/SCL lead holds the bus and stops the baro.

docs.title: Bill of materials
docs.text: JLCPCB assembles the 32 surface-mount parts (21 BOM lines). You buy and solder the through-hole parts yourself. LCSC stock was checked on 28 Oct 2026. docs.title: Hand-soldered (through-hole)
docs.text:
Qty Part LCSC Where 1 2x20 female socket, 8.5 mm tall C5124634 U1 (Pi). Must be the standard 8.5 mm height. 1 2x9 male header C42372517 J1 1 2x8 male header C32713281 J7 1 1x7 male header C32713273 J18 3 1x6 male header C32713272 J8, J11, J17 6 1x4 male header C32713270 J6, J9, J12, J23, J24, J25 1 1x3 male header C32713269 J10 1 1x2 male header C32713268 J13 1 JST-XH 2-pin vertical, 2.5 mm C2908600 J20 1 m each 18 AWG silicone wire, red + black – J3 battery tap 1 kit 2.54 mm Dupont housings (1x4, 2x9) + crimp pins – Kakute harness 1 m 26–28 AWG silicone wire – Kakute harness 4 M2.5 standoffs, 10 mm or more, + screws – Board to frame 4 M2.5 standoffs, about 11 mm, + screws – Pi Zero (optional)

Male headers can all be snapped from long 2.54 mm breakaway strips instead of buying each size.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: The board is built around a Pi Zero W v1.1 and a Kakute H7 V1.5. Other parts work if they match the footprint, voltage and signal listed here. "Tested part" means designed and checked against datasheets; nothing has been flown on this board yet.

docs.title: Companion computer (U1 socket)
docs.text:
Board Fits Notes Raspberry Pi Zero W v1.1 Yes, the design target Mounts face down. Its 2x20 male header must be on the component side (as on a Zero WH). Raspberry Pi Zero WH Yes Header is already on top, which is what the face-down mount needs. Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W Yes Same 65 x 30 mm outline, 58 x 23 mm holes and 40-pin pinout. Faster (quad core), and draws more power, up to about 0.6 A busy; the 5 V rail has the headroom. Raspberry Pi Zero / Zero 1.3 (no wireless) Yes Works electrically; no Wi-Fi for setup or data download. Pi Zero with the header soldered underneath No, as is Pins would point away from the socket. Use a Pi with the header on top. Pi 3, 4, 5, Pi 3A+ and other full-size boards No Different size and hole pattern. The Pi 5 also maps its UARTs differently.

The socket must be the standard 8.5 mm tall 2x20 female header (LCSC C5124634) so the face-down Pi sits at the designed height.

docs.title: Flight controller (J1, J23, J24, J25)
docs.text:
• Holybro Kakute H7 V1.5: the design target. The four header rows copy its pad names, so the Dupont harness runs straight across.
  • Kakute H7 V1 / V1.2: same 35 x 35 mm size and 30.5 mm M3 holes. The bottom 6-pin connector's pin order differs on V1.2 drawings, so check pad labels before wiring. V1 uses a BMP280 baro; flash the same KakuteH7 target.
  • Kakute H7 v2 and Kakute H7 Mini: they fit the holes, but the pad layout and firmware target differ. You would need your own harness map.
  • Any other 30.5 x 30.5 mm M3 flight controller: it mounts, because the FC is joined by a wire harness rather than plug-to-plug. Map each header pin to that FC's pads by function (5V, GND, UART TX/RX, SDA/SCL, servo out).

docs.title: ESC
docs.text: The ESC is not on this board. The Tekko32 F4 65A (AM32) sits on the S500's lower power plate. Its 8-pin cable comes up through the slot in the carrier straight to the Kakute's ESC port. Any 4-in-1 ESC with a JST-SH 8-pin cable that the Kakute supports works the same way. The board only taps battery voltage from the ESC pads (J3).

docs.title: Peripherals
docs.text: Function Tested part Also works Watch out for GPS + compass (J8) TBS M10Q with Q5883 compass Any 5 V GPS with UART + I2C compass (e.g. Matek M10Q-5883, Holybro M10) J8 order is TX RX GND VCC SCL SDA, matching the TBS pads. Lead colours vary by maker; wire by function, never by colour. Telemetry radio (J9) SiK Telemetry Radio V3, 433 MHz, 100 mW Any 5 V UART radio (915 MHz SiK, other MAVLink radios) UK law limits 433 MHz to 10 mW: set the radio's TXPOWER to 10. High-power radios (RFD900x) can draw close to 1 A and should not run off 5V_FC. RC receiver (J10) FlySky FS-iA10B on iBUS Receivers with iBUS, SBUS or PPM on one signal wire J10 carries only the FC's R3 input. Two-way protocols that need a TX line (CRSF, ELRS telemetry) won't send telemetry back through it. Rangefinder (J11) Benewake TF-Luna, I2C mode (CFG grounded), address 0x10 Other 5 V I2C lidars ArduPilot supports Shares the I2C bus with the baro and compass. A miswired I2C device stops the baro. Payload servo (J13 + Kakute M5) 9 g micro servo Any 5 V servo under about 1 A stall Power comes from 5V_AUX, never from the FC. Camera None fitted Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3 or v1.3 with a 15-to-22-pin Zero cable The carrier has no camera mount. The Pi's camera connector is on its short edge opposite the SD card, facing the board. Check the latch can open before you commit to a camera.

docs.title: Battery
docs.text: Designed for a 6S pack, 18 to 25.2 V (Li-ion or LiPo). The battery tap fuses and TVS are rated 30 V, so packs above 6S are not supported.

docs.title: Connectors and pinouts
docs.text: Every header is 2.54 mm pitch. Pin 1 is the square pad, and every pin is named on the silkscreen. On the upright 1-row headers along the left and right edges, pin 1 is the end nearest the nose. "TX" and "RX" in each table are from the peripheral's side, so the device's TX always lands on an FC RX.

docs.title: J3 VBAT TAP
docs.text: Two solder-wire pads, marked "6S 18-25.2V". Run 18 AWG silicone wire from the ESC's battery pads. Pin 1 (+) is VBAT, pin 2 (−) is GND. Worst-case draw is about 3.1 A: 1.1 A into the buck at full 5 V load from a flat pack, plus 2 A on J20.

docs.title: J20 VBAT OUT
docs.text: JST-XH 2-pin, vertical. Pin 1 = OUT+ (battery through F2, 2 A hold), pin 2 = OUT− (GND). Use it for an accessory that wants raw battery voltage, and check the accessory accepts 25.2 V.

docs.title: J6 PWR SPARE
docs.text: Pin Net Notes 1 5V_AUX Board buck, shared with the Pi and servo 2 GND 3 5V_FC Kakute's 5 V; keep loads small (current limit unconfirmed) 4 GND

docs.title: J13 SERVO 5V
docs.text:
Pin Net 1 (+) 5V_AUX 2 (−) GND

J13 carries servo power only. The servo's signal wire goes to M5 on the Kakute's 8-pin ESC port 2 plug (port 2 = B+, R7, GND, NC, M5, M6, M7, M8), not to the carrier. Set SERVO5_FUNCTION to 28 (Gripper).

docs.title: J8 GPS (TBS M10Q)
docs.text:
The order matches the M10Q's own pad labels.

Pin Silk Net Kakute pad 1 TX UART6_FC_RX R6 2 RX UART6_FC_TX T6 3 GND GND GND 4 5V_FC 5V_FC 5V 5 SCL I2C_SCL SCL 6 SDA I2C_SDA SDA

docs.title: J11 TF-Luna (I2C mode)
docs.text:
Pins 1–6 follow the TF-Luna's own pin order. CFG is tied to GND on the board, which puts the TF-Luna in I2C mode (address 0x10).

Pin Silk Net 1 5V_FC 5V_FC 2 SDA I2C_SDA 3 SCL I2C_SCL 4 GND GND 5 CFG=GND GND 6 MUX nc Not connected

docs.title: J12 I2C SPARE
docs.text: Pin 1 5V_FC, pin 2 GND, pin 3 SCL, pin 4 SDA. Same FC I2C bus as the GPS compass, TF-Luna and the Kakute's baro, so a new device must not use an address already on the bus.

docs.title: J9 SiK radio (UART4)
docs.text: Pin Silk Net Kakute pad 1 5V_FC 5V_FC 5V 2 GND GND GND 3 TX UART4_FC_RX R4 4 RX UART4_FC_TX T4

docs.title: J10 RC receiver (iBUS)
docs.text:
A standard servo-lead order, S + −.

Pin Silk Net Kakute pad 1 IBUS RC_IBUS R3 2 5V_FC 5V_FC 5V 3 GND GND GND

docs.title: J17 FC SPARE
docs.text:
Kakute signals not used yet.

Pin Silk Net Kakute pad 1 T3 UART3_TX_SPARE T3 2 RSSI RSSI_SPARE Rsi 3 3V3_FC 3V3_FC 3V3 4 GND GND GND 5 BUZ- BUZZER_SPARE Z− 6 LED LED_SPARE LED (addressable LED data)

BUZ− is the Kakute's switched buzzer return: a buzzer goes between a 5 V pin and BUZ−.

docs.title: Pi expansion headers (3.3 V logic only)
docs.text:
Warning

These pins go straight to the Pi's GPIO, which is not 5 V tolerant. Never put 5 V on a signal pin here.

docs.title: J7 PI GPIO
docs.text:
Odd pins in the left column, even pins in the right.

Pin Signal Pin Signal 1 3V3 (Pi) 2 GND 3 SDA1 (GPIO2) 4 SCL1 (GPIO3) 5 GPIO4 6 GPIO17 7 GPIO27 8 GPIO22 9 GPIO23 10 GPIO24 11 GPIO25 12 GPIO5 13 GPIO6 14 GPIO12 15 GPIO13 16 GPIO26

The Pi's I2C1 on J7 is a separate bus from the FC's I2C. It is not connected to the GPS or the TF-Luna.

docs.title: J18 PI SPI0
docs.text: Pin Signal 1 3V3 (Pi) 2 GND 3 MOSI (GPIO10) 4 MISO (GPIO9) 5 SCLK (GPIO11) 6 CE0 (GPIO8) 7 CE1 (GPIO7)

docs.title: Kakute harness headers
docs.text: The Kakute's pads are flat solder pads, so it joins the board by a short harness: 26–28 AWG silicone wire soldered to the pads, crimped into 2.54 mm Dupont housings at the other end. Each header copies the Kakute's pad layout one to one, so each wire runs straight across. Leave the wires slack so the Kakute stays soft-mounted.

Pin Kakute pin Net Goes to 1 9V Do not wire Nothing 2 T1 UART1_FC_TX Pi pin 10 (GPIO15 RXD) 3 R1 UART1_FC_RX Pi pin 8 (GPIO14 TXD) 4 G GND GND

The JST's second G and R6 pins are left unconnected (R6 is already on J1).

docs.title: U1 Pi Zero socket
docs.text:
A 2x20 female socket, 8.5 mm tall. The Pi plugs on face down: its header is on the component side, pins pointing at the carrier. Pin 1 (3V3, marked "< PIN 1") is at the right end, on the row nearer the rear edge. The SD card is on the right and the USB/HDMI edge is at the rear.

Danger

Fitting the Pi face up mirrors the pinout and puts 5 V on the wrong pins.

Pins the board uses (the rest are free, and most are on J7 and J18):

Pi pin Pi signal Board net Goes to 1, 17 3V3 3V3_PI J7.1, J18.1 2, 4 5V 5V_AUX Board buck (powers the Pi) 6, 9, 14, 20, 25, 30, 34, 39 GND GND 8 GPIO14 TXD UART1_FC_RX Kakute R1 via J25.3 10 GPIO15 RXD UART1_FC_TX Kakute T1 via J25.2 12 GPIO18 LED_BATT_LO D7 red, B-L 35 GPIO19 LED_BATT_HI D5 green, B-H 36 GPIO16 LED_PI_ACTIVE D3 green, PI 38 GPIO20 LED_DATA D4 yellow, DATA 40 GPIO21 LED_BATT_MID D6 yellow, B-M 27, 28 ID_SD, ID_SC Not connected

docs.text:
Seven LEDs sit in a row behind the buck, labelled "STATUS". From left to right:

docs.title: Limitations and open items
docs.text: The board has not been built or flown yet. These points are unconfirmed or are design limits to know about.

docs.title: Unconfirmed
docs.text:
• Kakute 5 V current limit. Everything on 5V_FC (GPS, SiK, receiver, TF-Luna, spares) shares it. Keep high-current loads on 5V_AUX.
  • Kakute pad pitch against the J1/J23/J24/J25 header layout. Check with a 1:1 print before crimping the harness.
  • Lead order of your SiK and TF-Luna cables, and the M10Q's wire colours. Wire by the labels on the device, never by colour.
  • Cover fit: Kakute stack height (under 21 mm assumed) and Dupont plug height (under 20 mm assumed).
  • Camera clearance: the carrier has no camera mount, and nobody has checked that the Pi's camera connector latch can open with the Pi face down.

docs.title: Design limits
docs.text:
• 6S only (18 to 25.2 V). The fuses and TVS are rated 30 V.
  • No on-board enable or low-voltage cut-off for the 5 V buck: it runs whenever the battery is connected.
  • No 9 V or 12 V outputs (removed in V1.0 to cut cost). The Kakute's 9V pad is not brought to the board.
  • J10 has only the R3 receive line, so two-way RC protocols can't send telemetry back through it. T3 is available on J17 if needed.
  • The Pi's GPIO16, 18, 19, 20 and 21 drive the status LEDs, so they aren't free for other uses.

docs.title: Small mismatches in the design files
docs.text:
• The J3 schematic value says 20 AWG; use 18 AWG, as the assembly notes and BOM say.
  • The values of J1, J23, J24, J25 and U1 still say "(JLC THT)". Since the hand-solder change they are not fitted by JLC.

docs.title: Mounting and cover
docs.text:
The board has three hole patterns. Coordinates are in mm from the board's front-left corner, x to the right and y towards the rear.

Holes Pattern Size Positions (x, y) Use H5–H8, "FRAME M2.5" 48.5 mm square Oval slots 4.2 x 2.7 mm (23.25, 34.0) (71.75, 34.0) (23.25, 82.5) (71.75, 82.5) Board to the S500 centre plate H1–H4 30.5 mm square 3.2 mm (M3) (32.25, 43.0) (62.75, 43.0) (32.25, 73.5) (62.75, 73.5) Kakute H7 stack Pi holes 58 x 23 mm 2.75 mm (M2.5) (17.93, 90.53) (75.93, 90.53) (17.93, 113.53) (75.93, 113.53) Pi Zero support

  • To the frame: four M2.5 standoffs, at least 10 mm, through the frame slots. The slots are oval so they can line up with the frame's holes. Trim all through-hole leads to 1.5 mm or less underneath so nothing touches the plate. The two rear frame slots sit under the edge of the Pi, so fit their screws before the Pi.
  • Kakute: on its own rubber grommets with M3 screws through H1–H4. Its arrow must point at the nose, matching the silkscreen arrow ("FRONT = KAKUTE ARROW").
  • ESC cable slot: a 14 x 5 mm obround cut-out centred at (50.5, 47.6), inside the Kakute square. The ESC's 8-pin cable comes up through it from the lower plate. A 65 mm cable reaches.
  • Pi Zero: plugs into U1 face down; its component side sits about 11 mm above the board (8.5 mm socket plus the header's spacer). If you add M2.5 standoffs at the Pi holes, measure that gap first. No carrier parts sit under the Pi, and the tallest Pi part (mini-HDMI, about 3.2 mm) leaves about 7.8 mm.

docs.title: Moisture cover
docs.text:
A 3D-printable lid is in the project folder under maame/cover/: MaameDrone_V1.0_cover.stl (ready to print), .step for CAD and the .py source.

  • Size: 102 x 126.5 x 36.6 mm outside, 30 mm clear inside. The skirt hangs 3 mm below the board so water drips off the edge.
  • Print: PETG or ASA (PLA softens in the sun), roof down, no supports, about 60 g. White or natural filament lets the status LEDs glow through the 0.6 mm roof panel.
  • Mount: swap the 4 nuts on top of the Kakute for M3 male-female standoffs, then fix the lid with 4 x M3x14 screws and rubber washers. Standoff length = 22 mm minus the height of the Kakute's screw tops above the board.
  • Cable exits: open slots for J3, J8, J11, J13 (left) and J9, J10 (right). J20, J12, J6, J17, J18 and J7 have 0.6 mm knock-outs; cut one out only when you use that header.
  • Sealing: close cable gaps with foam tape or silicone, but don't make it airtight, which traps condensation. For damp conditions also conformal-coat the board, masking the headers, Pi socket, fuses and JST socket.

Unconfirmed

The lid assumes the Kakute stack is under 21 mm and the Dupont plugs with their cable bend are under 20 mm tall.

docs.title: Power
docs.text:
The board has four separate supply rails and a fused battery output. Only 5V_AUX is made on the board; the others come from the Kakute and the Pi.

Rail Source Limit Feeds VBAT Battery via J3 F1 and F2, 2 A hold / 4 A trip each Buck input (F1), J20 (F2) 5V_AUX U2 TPS54360B buck, 600 kHz 3.5 A Pi Zero, servo (J13), J6 pin 1, AUX5V LED; 470 µF + 2 x 47 µF on the output 5V_FC Kakute's 5 V regulator Unconfirmed; keep to GPS, radio, receiver and lidar J1, J23, J24 harness pins, J8, J9, J10, J11, J12, J6 pin 3, FC5V LED 3V3_FC Kakute's 3.3 V Small; logic only J17 pin 3 3V3_PI Pi Zero's regulator Small; logic only J7 pin 1, J18 pin 1

All grounds are one common GND net.

  • Protection: F1 and F2 are 30 V resettable PTC fuses. D9 (SMBJ30A) clamps spikes on the buck input. The buck has no enable or undervoltage cut-off divider; its EN pin floats on purpose, so it runs whenever the battery is connected.
  • The Kakute's own power arrives over the ESC's 8-pin cable (B+), not through the carrier. The board does not connect to the Kakute's B+, Vo, Vi or 9V pads.

Never join the rails

5V_AUX and 5V_FC meet only at GND. Don't bridge them with a jumper or a device that takes 5 V on two pins, or the two regulators will fight. The same goes for 3V3_FC and 3V3_PI.

docs.title: Firmware and software
docs.text: The board needs ArduCopter on the Kakute (KakuteH7 target, 4.6 or newer), one Lua script on the FC's SD card, and two Python modules on the Pi. All files are in the project folder under maame/ardupilot and maame/pi.

docs.title: Flight controller (ArduPilot)
docs.text:
Flash the KakuteH7 target, not KakuteH7v2: the V1.5 board has an SPA06 barometer that only the KakuteH7 build drives, from Copter 4.6. Flash arducopter_with_bl.hex over DFU with Betaflight Configurator (Mission Planner 1.3.76 cannot flash over DFU).

Parameter Value Why SERIAL1_PROTOCOL 2 (MAVLink2) Pi Zero on UART1 SERIAL1_BAUD 921 921600 baud to the Pi SERIAL3_PROTOCOL 23 (RCIN) FS-iA10B iBUS on R3 SERIAL4_PROTOCOL / BAUD 2 / 57 SiK radio on UART4 SERIAL6_PROTOCOL 5 (GPS) TBS M10Q on UART6 BRD_ALT_CONFIG 1 Makes R6/T6 a UART; without it the GPS is never found RNGFND1_TYPE 25 TF-Luna on I2C (address 0x10) SERVO5_FUNCTION 28 (Gripper) Payload servo on M5 BATT_MONITOR 4 Tekko32 analog voltage + current BATT_VOLT_MULT / BATT_AMP_PERVLT 11.0 / 59.5 KakuteH7 defaults for the Tekko32 sensors SCR_ENABLE 1 Runs the arming-gate script SCR_USER1 0 (1 = bypass) Bypass the Pi gate for manual test flights SCR_USER2 1 Pi lost in flight: RTL from GUIDED, keep flying AUTO (0 = warn, 2 = RTL from AUTO too)

Reboot the Kakute after changing the SERIAL and BRD_ALT_CONFIG values.

docs.title: Arming gate (Lua)
docs.text:
maame_pi_gate.lua blocks arming until the Pi reports it is ready. Copy it to APM/scripts/ on the Kakute's SD card, and copy the modules/MAVLink/ folder to APM/scripts/modules/MAVLink/.

It listens for a HEARTBEAT from component 191 with status ACTIVE. If none arrives for 3 s, arming fails with "Pi companion not ready", and in flight it applies the SCR_USER2 action. A script error also keeps arming blocked.

docs.title: Pi Zero
docs.text:
• Serial port: the Pi talks to the FC on /dev/serial0 (GPIO14 TXD, GPIO15 RXD) at 921600. In raspi-config turn the serial login shell off and the serial port on. Add dtoverlay=disable-bt to /boot/config.txt so the full PL011 UART is used; the mini UART drifts at this speed on a Pi Zero W.
  • maame_ready.py: the CompanionLink class. It sends the heartbeat every 0.5 s (STANDBY until set_ready(True), then ACTIVE), reads the FC's mode, and pilot_has_control() tells mission code to stop commanding when the pilot is not in GUIDED or AUTO. Needs pymavlink.
  • maame_leds.py: the StatusLeds class drives the five Pi status LEDs from MAVLink data. Needs gpiozero.
Pi GPIO Label Colour Meaning GPIO16 PI Green Companion script running; blinks if the FC goes quiet for 3 s GPIO20 DATA Yellow Flashes on each MAVLink message in or out GPIO19 B-H Green Battery 50 % or more (or above 3.70 V per cell) GPIO21 B-M Yellow Battery 25 to 50 % (3.50 to 3.70 V per cell) GPIO18 B-L Red Battery low; flashes on the FC's low-battery failsafe

All five LEDs are active high (GPIO, resistor, LED, GND). Those five GPIOs are taken; don't reuse them for anything else.

Minimal use:

from maame_ready import CompanionLink
from maame_leds import StatusLeds

link = CompanionLink("/dev/serial0", 921600, leds=StatusLeds())
link.wait_for_fc()
# ... run self-checks ...
link.set_ready(True)
while True:
    link.tick()
    if link.pilot_has_control():
        continue  # do not send commands
    # ... mission logic ...
